analysis_steps.goal: Fit line profiles per pixel and azimuthal average

method.value: Fit saturated-core opacity profile for CO, hyperfine Gaussian fit in CLASS for CN, Gaussian for CS; spectra shifted by local Keplerian velocity before azimuthal averaging

evidence.quote: Using the ‘hyperfine’ mode in `CLASS` the hyperfine components were simultaneously fit with Gaussian profiles.

key_parameters.value: Keplerian model with M*=0.69 Msun, i=7 deg for shifting

evidence.quote: We used for this the best fit Keplerian model assuming a stellar mass of $0.69~M_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$ and $i = 7\ensuremath{^\circ}$

assumptions.value: CN hyperfine components from same region, main component optically thick

evidence.quote: Under the assumption that all hyperfine components arise from the same region in the disk and that the main component is optically thick

validation.value: Channel resolution bias estimated ~2% (CO, CN) and 3.5% (CS) and corrected

evidence.quote: we estimate that the bias on the measured $\Delta V$ would be $\approx 2~\%$ for CO and CN and $\approx 3.5~\%$ for CS.

method.value: LIME models of Gorti disk without turbulence at several inclinations, synthetic observations in CASA, power-law fit to linewidth difference

evidence.quote: Differences in the resulting line width at each pixel between an inclined disk and a face on disk were attributed to Keplerian broadening.

key_parameters.value: Direct methods only for r>40 au; inclinations 0,5,6,7,8,9 deg

evidence.quote: In the following ‘direct’ methods we only consider the disk outside 40 au.
the radial distribution of differences in linewidths was well fit by a power law outside of 40 au

validation.value: 12CO and C18O differences smaller than quoted uncertainties

evidence.quote: The differences between the $^{12}$CO and C$^{18}$O cases were smaller than these quoted uncertainties.

method.value: Subtract thermal width from corrected linewidth using Tex from line profile

evidence.quote: With a known $T_{\rm kin}$ a simple subtraction of the thermal broadening component leaves $v_{\rm turb}$.

assumptions.value: CO and CN thermalised, Tex = Tkin

evidence.quote: we make the assumption that both CO and CN lines are thermalised so that $T_{\rm ex}$ = $T_{\rm kin}$ $= T$.

validation.value: CN beyond ~140 au excluded due to supra-thermal Tex > Tkin^max

evidence.quote: Outside of $r \sim 140$ au, CN shows signs of non-LTE effects

findings_qualitative.value: Co-spatial CN/CS assumption fails beyond ~100 au; CO, CN, CS likely trace different vertical layers

evidence.quote: These pieces of evidence suggest CO, CN and CS each trace distinct vertical regions in the disk

claims.hypothesis: Can turbulence in TW Hya be directly measured with ALMA line widths?
claims.experiment: Single-molecule and co-spatial direct methods on CO, CN, CS beyond 40 au
claims.finding: Turbulence is comparable to or below MRI predictions; values best treated as upper limits

evidence.quote: the analysis of the possible sources of errors shows that these numbers should most likely be interpreted as upper limits.

claims.result: No solution between ~100 and 180 au; parametric temperatures differ
claims.finding: Co-spatial assumption fails over much of disk

evidence.quote: the assumption fails absolutely between $100 \lesssim r \lesssim 180$ au

claims.result: 7-10% calibration gives sensitivity ≳0.2 cs; 3% gives ≳0.07 cs
claims.finding: Absolute flux calibration is the limiting factor

evidence.quote: We demonstrate that absolute flux calibration is and will be the limiting factor in all studies of turbulence using a single molecule.

why_this_data.value: Face-on, nearest disk minimizes Keplerian shear

evidence.quote: TW Hya provides the best opportunity to directly detect turbulent broadening as the impact of Keplerian shear for such face-on disks is minimized

limitations_admitted.value: Direct methods limited to r>40 au by beam smear; CN non-LTE beyond ~140 au

evidence.quote: The two direct methods were limited to the outer $r > 40$ au disk due to beam smear.

referee_caveats_inferred: Parametric fit uncertainties are formal and underestimated
Single epoch with 7% flux scale uncertainty
